summary: The pin bump, the Qt property metadata plumbing, the `pragma` alias, and the QML tests are sound. The `.h` workaround in `update_file` is not safe as written. It copies the scan call from `scan_workspace` but drops the `partial` and `schema_incompatible` handling and the FTS re-check, so one unreadable file anywhere in the workspace makes every header edit roll back and every header read fail. It also runs one full forced re-extraction per header on the offline reconcile and watcher batch paths, so a pull that touches 30 headers costs 30 full scans at startup. The trigger fires for every `.h`, including pure C projects where `update` was already correct. Smaller items: `StructuralFact.metadata` now inflates `facts --json` for every category, and one malformed `metadata_json` row aborts the whole facts query. No build or test commands could be run in this session; the archive hashes and the documented test counts are not independently verified.

findings.title: scan_header_file drops scan_workspace's error handling, so a partial scan rolls back every header edit
findings.body: `scan_header_file` builds its own `scan --force` call and returns any non-zero exit as an error. `scan_workspace` treats exit 1 with a `partial` stderr as a warning and a `schema_incompatible` stderr as a rebuild, and it runs `ensure_fts_index_path` after the scan. The header path does none of this. `commit_file_edit` rolls the file back on any `update_file` error. Result: one unreadable file anywhere in the workspace makes every `.h` `edit_file` and `replace_symbol_body` roll back with `SyncWithRollback`, and every `.h` read tool call errors through `ensure_fresh_file`. The FTS tables are also not re-checked after a forced full re-extraction the way they are after every other scan.
findings.recommendation: Call `scan_workspace(workspace, db_path, true)` from `scan_header_file` instead of building the args again, then keep the hash check. Add a test with one `chmod 000` file plus a header edit and assert the edit is not rolled back.

findings.title: Offline reconcile and the watcher run one full forced scan per changed header
findings.body: `reconcile_offline_edits` with 50 or fewer changes calls `update_file` for each added and modified path. The watcher does the same per debounce window. Each `.h` in those lists now runs a full forced re-extraction of the whole workspace, in series. A pull or checkout that touches 30 Qt headers costs 30 full scans before the first tool call answers, and 51 changes would have cost one cheaper non-forced scan. The audit lists the watcher and offline paths as covered, but the cost multiplies there.
findings.recommendation: In both batch loops, if any pending path is a `.h`, run one `scan_workspace(force=true)` for the batch and skip the per-file loop. Apply the same rule in watcher.rs lines 119 to 131. Add a reconcile test with two modified headers that counts extractor runs.

findings.title: The workaround fires for every .h, including C projects where update was already correct
findings.body: The trigger is the file extension only. A C codebase with thousands of headers now pays a full workspace re-extraction for every header refresh or edit, even though `update` classifies those files correctly. The upstream defect only affects headers that a full scan reports as `cpp`.
findings.recommendation: Read the stored `files.language` before the update. Use the forced scan only when the stored language is `cpp` or the header is not yet indexed. Keep `update` for everything else.

findings.title: A header the scan ignores now fails with TargetNotIndexed after a full scan and rolls back the edit
findings.body: After the forced scan, a missing `files` row or a hash mismatch returns `TargetNotIndexed`. A `.h` under a gitignored or `.julieignore`d path, or under a hard-excluded directory such as `build/` (Qt `ui_*.h` and `moc_*.h` live there), is never indexed by a scan. `ensure_fresh_file` sees no row, marks it dirty, runs the full scan, and then errors; `file_skeleton_op` propagates that error and `commit_file_edit` rolls the edit back. The previous `update --file` path handled such a file directly. Only the missing-file case is tested.
findings.recommendation: Before the forced scan, check the path against the same ignore matcher the watcher builds (watcher.rs lines 51 to 57) and against `is_hard_excluded`; fall back to `update` or return `Ok(())` for ignored paths. Add a test for a header under `build/`.

findings.title: Each header edit likely triggers a second full scan from the watcher
findings.body: `commit_file_edit` runs the forced scan synchronously. The watcher fires 150 ms after the write. On any real repository the first scan is still running, so the watcher's `ensure_fresh_file` reads the old WAL snapshot, sees a stale hash, and starts a second forced scan. That scan hits the SQLite write lock, retries with backoff for about 3 s, then either runs a redundant full re-extraction or fails silently. Not observed in this session; inferred from the timing in the code.
findings.recommendation: Have the watcher skip a path whose disk hash already matches a scan in progress, or guard forced scans with a process-wide in-progress flag so a second request waits and re-checks freshness instead of scanning again.

findings.title: StructuralFact.metadata is serialized for every fact, inflating facts --json for all categories
findings.body: `metadata` has no `skip_serializing_if`, and the CLI prints the facts vector straight to JSON. Every route, config, SQL, and QML fact now carries its full `metadata_json` object in `--json` output, not only Qt property facts. `ReferenceSite.occurrences` shows the established pattern. `Deserialize` without `#[serde(default)]` also rejects JSON written by earlier builds.
findings.recommendation: Add `#[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]` on `metadata`, and consider loading metadata only for `cpp.qt_property.v1` rows if JSON size matters.

findings.title: One malformed metadata_json row aborts the whole facts query
findings.body: The row mapper parses `metadata_json` with `serde_json::from_str` and turns a parse failure into a row error, which fails the entire `find_structural_facts_scoped` call. Before this change the query only used `json_extract`, which tolerates bad rows.
findings.recommendation: Treat a parse failure as `None` (`.ok()`), optionally with a `warn!`, so one bad row does not hide every other fact.

findings.title: Pin bump and behavior change have no release notes or version bump
findings.body: Release archives bundle the pinned extractor, and `docs/RELEASING.md` expects `docs/release-notes/vX.Y.Z.md` per release. This bundle changes the pin and adds a user-visible cost (full re-extraction per header) but adds no release note and no version bump. Until a release ships, plugin users download the 1.6.0 archive with julie-extract 3.3.0 while source builds require 3.3.1; the runtime warning path covers that mismatch. The six archive SHA-256 values could not be verified offline.
findings.recommendation: Draft the next release note with the pin change and the header re-extraction cost, and verify the six hashes against the GitHub release digests before tagging.

next_steps: Replace the hand-built scan in `scan_header_file` with `scan_workspace(workspace, db_path, true)` and keep the hash check.
Narrow the trigger to headers whose stored language is `cpp` or that are not yet indexed.
Batch the forced scan in `reconcile_offline_edits` and the watcher: one scan per batch that contains a header.
Add `#[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]` to `StructuralFact.metadata` and make a bad `metadata_json` row parse to `None`.
Add tests: header edit with one unreadable sibling file does not roll back; reconcile with two modified headers runs one scan; header under `build/` does not error.
Run `cargo test -p code-kb-core --test freshness_test --test qt_cpp_test --test qt_qml_test`, then the workspace gate and clippy.
Verify the six archive SHA-256 values in `scripts/julie-pins.json` against the v3.3.1 release digests.

evidence.observation: `scan_header_file` builds `scan --root --db [--parent-pid] --force` itself, propagates every `execute_julie_extract` error, and does not call `ensure_fts_index_path`.
`scan_workspace` treats `partial` stderr with exit 1 as a warning, rebuilds on `schema_incompatible`, and runs `ensure_fts_index_path` after every scan. None of this reaches the header path.
Any `update_file` error after the atomic write triggers a rollback of the file and returns `SyncWithRollback`.
Reconcile with 50 or fewer changes calls `update_file` per added and per modified path in series; more than 50 changes run one non-forced `scan_workspace`.
Watcher: more than 50 paths run one scan; otherwise each path goes through `ensure_fresh_file` then `update_file`, so each `.h` costs a full forced scan.
Debounce window is 150 ms, shorter than a full forced scan on a real repository.
Extractor lock collisions retry five times with backoff (100 to 1600 ms), then fail.
The forced-scan trigger checks only that the DB file exists and the extension is `h`, not the stored language.
After the scan, a missing `files` row or a hash mismatch returns `TargetNotIndexed`.
`ensure_fresh_file` marks a file with no `files` row as dirty and calls `update_file`, so an ignored header runs the forced scan and then errors.
`file_skeleton_op` propagates any `ensure_fresh_file` error with `?`.
`build`, `dist`, `target`, and `vendor` are hard-excluded directories; Qt generated headers commonly live under `build/`.
`ReferenceSite.occurrences` uses `skip_serializing_if`; the new `StructuralFact.metadata` field has no serde attribute.
`facts --json` serializes the `StructuralFact` vector directly, so every fact now carries its metadata object.
Column 11 is `sf.metadata_json` (column 10 is `display_key`), so the index is correct; a JSON parse failure becomes a row error that fails the whole query.
`javascript.qml_directive.v1` has no leading or trailing dot, so `matches_family` and `family_clause` treat it as an exact id match; the alias change is correct.
`qt_property_details` renders only for `cpp.qt_property.v1`, prints string values raw and other JSON values via `to_string`; consistent with the unit and integration tests.
The header test covers language preservation on a same-size edit and the missing-file error; it does not cover an ignored header, a partial scan, or batch reconcile cost.
The JavaScript QML directive test asserts exactly one `pragma` fact on line 1 for a file with both `.pragma` and `.import`, so the alias does not pull in import directives.
The synthetic alias fixture expects `pragma` to map to `qml.pragma.v1` only; it has no JS directive facts, so it stays consistent with the alias change.
The build guard reads the pin from `scripts/julie-pins.json`; no hard-coded extractor version remains outside `PINNED_JULIE_VERSION`.
`pinned_version_matches_the_pins_file` ties `PINNED_JULIE_VERSION` to the JSON `version`, both now 3.3.1.
Release archives bundle the restored pinned `julie-extract`, so users receive 3.3.1 only after the next release.
The release process expects a `docs/release-notes/vX.Y.Z.md` file; this bundle adds none.
Both AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md move from blob 0bf421b to e4252e8 in the diff header, so the byte-for-byte sync contract holds.
